business_scope.primary_industry_name: Foreign Market Feasibility Study and Regulatory Licensing Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Cook Islands (self-governing state in free association with New Zealand)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law) with local statutory modifications; unitary sovereign framework within the Realm of New Zealand, exercising devolved legislative authority over company formation and financial regulation.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus)
New Zealand – Cook Islands constitutional and financial regulatory cooperation instruments (free association status)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1981-82 (as amended), Financial Supervisory Commission Act 2004, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (as amended), and the Financial Supervision (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019; beneficial ownership obligations for international companies are administered by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission under the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / Authorized Certifying Officer in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed registered agent / Cook Islands compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, as applicable to the signatory's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or professional reference from a licensed regulated entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank or regulated professional services firm

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List, and the Cook Islands domestic AML/CFT watchlist; identification of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under the AML/CFT Act 2018, with mandatory verification of source of wealth and source of funds; all positive matches must be escalated to the Financial Supervisory Commission and may result in rejection or conditional engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission – International Companies Registry (online name reservation via licensed registered agent portal; website: https://www.fsc.gov.ck)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English or any language using Latin script; non-Latin script names require transliteration into English characters and an English translation. The name must end with a statutory suffix such as 'International', 'International Company', 'IC', 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', or 'Incorporated'. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant, through its licensed registered agent, may request reconsideration in writing within 14 business days, specifying the grounds of compliance. If the registry confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Financial Supervisory Commission's Appeals Committee within 28 days of the reconsideration decision. A further appeal lies to the High Court of the Cook Islands by way of judicial review. Alternatively, the applicant may re-submit a modified name with payment of a new reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered office: not permissible as a virtual address; the International Company must maintain a physical registered office in the Cook Islands, being the premises of a licensed registered agent. For offsite administrative operations, a virtual office may be used, but substantive commercial presence in the Cook Islands is not required as the company is restricted from carrying on business with local residents without a separate domestic business licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 10% estimated probability) for a non-resident, low-risk consultancy company; however, the Financial Supervisory Commission may carry out unannounced inspections of the licensed registered agent's premises and records on a risk-based AML/CFT assessment cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Te Tari Kamupene o Aotearoa), a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form 1, Companies Act 1993, First Schedule) filed electronically through the Companies Office online portal, together with the Company Constitution and the Consents to Appointment as Director and Shareholder (Forms 2 and 3 respectively), and the Residential Address Statements and Director Consent and Certification forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under New Zealand law. Shares of a company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 may be allotted without payment of a par value or premium because New Zealand operates a no-par-value share regime (s 42 and s 43). The company must, however, maintain a registered office in New Zealand at all times (s 186) and have at least one director who is resident in New Zealand or an external director resident in Australia under s 151(1). The company may be wholly owned and controlled by non-residents, and an International Company (IC) structure relying on tax-exempt offshore revenue streams must not derive New Zealand source income.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (CK_IC) — INWRITING, UNANIMOUS BOARD RESOLUTION UNDER SECTION 107 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: that the board approves the issue and allotment of one hundred (100) fully paid ordinary shares with no par value to the founding shareholder at an allotment price of NZD 1.00 per share, such subscription funds to remain in the company's bank account or to be settled by contractual rights of indemnity as determined by the board; that the directors adopt the Share Register and issue the certificates, if so resolved, in accordance with ss 83 and 87. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: that the registered office of the company be established at the address provided to the Registrar under s 186, namely [Registered Office Address, New Zealand], and that such address also constitute the address for service for civil and administrative proceedings under s 187, and that the Board authorize the engagement of a licensed chartered accountant or corporate services provider as the agent for New Zealand tax and regulatory filings. 3. APPOINTMENT OF FIRST DIRECTORS: that the persons whose names and authorizations were filed with the Application for Registration be and are hereby appointed as directors of the company, such appointment to take effect on the date of certification by the Registrar, and that the directors in office shall comply with directors' duties under ss 131, 133, 135, 136, 137 and 138. 4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: that [Chief Executive Officer], [Chief Financial Officer], and [Company Secretary] be and are hereby appointed as officers of the company with authority to execute banking mandates, sign contracts, and represent the company for the purposes of the Companies Register, the Inland Revenue Department, the Financial Markets Authority (where applicable), and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register. 5. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS: that the board approves the opening of a New Zealand corporate bank account and the activation of Wise Business and Banco De Credito wire transfer facilities to receive consultancy fee income and pay arm's-length operating expenses; that the AML/CFT compliance function adopts a low-risk standard customer due diligence policy for this Market Entry Consultancy business model. 6. STATUTORY RECORDS AND FINANCIAL REPORTING: that the company shall maintain complete statutory records at its registered office as required under ss 188-193, and that where the company is not large or is an exempt company pursuant to s 30 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013, the directors may elect exempt company financial reporting status subject to all shareholders' written agreement. 7. GOVERNANCE AND GENERAL AUTHORITY: that the Chairman of the Board is authorized to affix the common seal if adopted, and the resolution is declared to be passed as a written resolution effective from the date of the Certificate of Incorporation or, if earlier, the date signed by all shareholders having at that time the right to attend and vote at a general meeting. — PASSED THIS [DAY] DAY OF [MONTH], [YEAR]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct Name Reservation and Initial Regulatory Feasibility Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) and the NZBN Register (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a pre-incorporation search of the Companies Register and the NZBN register to confirm that the chosen company name, including the proposed name 'CK International Company Limited' or an alternate containing the term 'Limited', is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or reserved name as prohibited under s 22 and s 23 of the Companies Act 1993. Verify that the name does not contain any restricted word under the Companies Act 1993 (Restricted Company Names) Regulations 1996, such as 'Trust', 'Bank', or 'University'. Prepare and lodge an online Name Reservation application. For an International Company intended to be tax-exempt with offshore operations in agriculture or food origin consulting, also confirm that the word 'Overseas Market Entry Consult' is permitted and will not mislead as to the nature of the business. The name reservation, once approved, is generally valid for 20 working days and may be renewed once for an additional 20 working days upon payment of the relevant extension fee.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and up to three alternate names
Search result printouts from the New Zealand Companies Register and NZBN register
Statement of business purpose describing the ISIC 7020 market entry consultancy activity (foreign market feasibility study and regulatory licensing agency)
Reservation application form completed online with applicant identification details (name and email address)
Authorization letter from the intended ultimate beneficial owner appointing the applicant as agent for name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query or a notice of likely refusal on grounds of identity, confusion, or restricted words, the applicant may file a written response within 20 working days, amend the name by submitting a fresh reservation with a different distinguishing element, or appeal the decision by judicial review to the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. If the name reservation expires, a new reservation application may be submitted without prejudice and the formation timeline extended accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Company Constitution, Shareholder Consents and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office standard forms; legal counsel and notary public for execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Constitution of the International Company (CK_IC) under s 26 and First Schedule of the Companies Act 1993. The Constitution must address, at minimum: the share structure with no par value shares, share transfer restrictions, director appointment and removal procedures, director indemnity and insurance (subject to s 162), shareholder meetings, and the conflict of interest policy under s 161. Prepare the Shareholder Consent form and the Director Consent form, both to be executed in accordance with ss 158 and 159. The Director Consent must be accompanied by a certified statement that the director is not disqualified under s 151 (undischarged bankrupt, disqualification order, or prohibited by law). Collect the residential addresses of all directors for the Residential Address Statement which will be filed with the Registrar. All execution signatures shall be witnessed, and any overseas shareholder or director execution must be notarized and, where appropriate, apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention, since New Zealand is a party to that Convention.
required_dossiers: Company Constitution in English
Consent to Appointment as Shareholder (Form 2 equivalent)
Consent to Appointment as Director (Form 3) for each proposed director
Director Residential Address Statement for each director
Statutory Declaration by a director or shareholder under s 158 confirming compliance
Notarized and apostilled powers of attorney if any overseas shareholder executes by agent
Identity documents of each director and shareholder (passport copy, utility bill confirming residential address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the constitution for inconsistency with the Companies Act 1993, the company may file an amended constitution at any time via Form 5 (Company Constitution – alteration). If a consent form is incomplete or not witnessed properly, the applicant will receive an electronic query and may resubmit the corrected form within 10 working days. If a director fails the disqualification review, the applicant must substitute a qualified resident director and file a fresh consent and residential address statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Registration of the Company and Pay the Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE — electronic incorporation service at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the Application for Registration of a Company (Form 1) electronically through the Companies Office online portal. The submission must include the proposed company name, the Company Constitution, the address of the registered office and the address for service, the full list of directors and shareholders, the number of shares and their classes, the ultimate holding company disclosure if any, and the consent forms. Confirm that at least one director is resident in New Zealand (or is an external director resident in Australia under s 151(1)). Pay the official filing fee of NZD 105.40 (approximately USD 65) by credit card, Debit card, POLi, or bank account debit. Upon successful submission, the system issues a transactional acknowledgement and forwards the application to the Companies Office processing queue. The certificate is issued electronically after verification.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Application for Registration of a Company, completed online
Company Constitution attached as PDF
Director and shareholder consent forms
Residential address statements
Payment confirmation reference
Consent from the proposed registered office provider (if not owned by the company)
Company name reservation number issued in Step 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, the Companies Office will notify the applicant with a description of the defect. The applicant may correct the electronic form and resubmit without paying a second fee only if the correction is made prior to the first processing completion; otherwise a fresh application and new fee are required. The applicant may request a priority review by telephone or through the MBIE Registrar's service desk, or invoke the Registrar's power to grant a short extension for the filing under s 385(1).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the NZBN issuing system managed by MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a digitally executed Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and the date of incorporation, and the company is automatically assigned a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), which serves as the primary identifier for government and business transactions. Verify the details on the certificate, including the company name and number, and retrieve the electronic certificate from the Companies Office portal. Concurrently, apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number by submitting the prescribed application form (IR596) unless an offshore tax file number has been waived or a transitional certificate is obtained. For the International Company (IC) structure, also file a non-resident company status notice with Inland Revenue if the central management and control of the company is outside New Zealand, relying on s YD 2(2) of the Income Tax Act 2007, so that the company is treated as a non-resident qualifying company for New Zealand tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued electronically
Companies Register extract showing company number and NZBN
Application for IRD number (IR596) with corresponding incorporation certificate
Notice of foreign company status or non-resident status, if applicable
Consent from the directors to be listed as responsible persons on the NZBN record
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical error, the company may apply to the Registrar for correction under s 22(1)(c) of the Companies Act 1993. If the NZBN is not automatically assigned, the company may apply via the NZBN bulletin service by calling the MBIE NZBN Helpline. If the IRD number application is delayed, the applicant may file a written request for expedited processing with Inland Revenue; any delay will not invalidate the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Initial Governance Resolution, Open Bank Account and Register for Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; Inland Revenue Department (IRD); registered banks and licensed non-bank payment institutions (Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute a written resolution adopting the Pro Forma First Board Resolution set out in the incorporation legal framework, covering share capital subscription, adoption of the registered office, appointment of directors and officers, appointment of a company secretary, adoption of bank mandates, and approval of the operating bank account and payment rails (Wise B2B and SWIFT/Telegraphic bank wire). Open the corporate bank account in New Zealand; where the beneficial owner is a non-resident, the bank will conduct enhanced due diligence but the business model is rated as low AML/CFT risk. Register with the Inland Revenue for GST only if the company supplies services in New Zealand or if annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000; otherwise the company may remain unregistered for GST. Ensure the company has a valid director identification for the resident director (New Zealand Director Number) and file the ultimate holding company disclosure if more than 50% of the shares are held by an overseas entity. The directors must also file a financial reporting exemption election, if applicable, under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
First Board Resolution and minutes of the first board meeting
Share register and director register
Resident director's proof of identity and new zealand address
Business plan describing the ISIC 7020 market entry consultancy operations
AML/CFT compliance manual identifying the low risk rating
Bank mandate and signatory list executed by directors
IRD registration confirmation or IR596 acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account opening due to insufficient corporate documentation, the directors must complete the outstanding diligence items, provide the certificate of incorporation and proof of registered office, or switch to a secondary licensed bank. If the AML/CFT classification is challenged, the company may submit a revised risk assessment to the compliant entity supervisor (Reserve Bank of New Zealand) for review. Any defect in the resolution may be cured by a subsequent written shareholder resolution under s 122 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Building Safety, Fire Safety and Health and Safety Compliance for the Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); local territorial authority building consent department; WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the commercial lease for the registered office and obtain a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) from the territorial authority where the premises exceed the exemption threshold or where the building holds a compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004. Retain the annual fire safety certification, such as the inspection of fire suppression systems, emergency lighting, exit signage, and fire alarm testing. Conduct a workplace health and safety induction for all employees and consultants, prepare a hazard register, appoint a health and safety representative, and display the health and safety policy; maintain accident records for WorkSafe inspection. For a consultancy business with no manufacturing or industrial emissions, no environmental impact assessment, discharge permit, or industrial site license is required; nevertheless, local council waste disposal and water/stormwater discharge obligations must be met.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease agreement for the registered office
Building Warrant of Fitness certificate (where compliance schedule applies)
Fire evacuation scheme approved by FENZ (if the premises require it under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017)
Annual fire system record and test certificates
Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 policy manual
Hazard register and workplace induction log
Trade waste discharge permit from the local authority (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the territorial authority records a compliance defect in the Building Warrant of Fitness, the building owner must cure the defect within 30 days and the company may serve a notice of the rectification on the council. If FENZ issues a compliance letter for unsafe evacuation, the tenant may implement interim risk mitigation and file an amended evacuation scheme without penalty if done immediately. If Worksafe issues a prohibition or improvement notice, the company shall establish a health and safety committee, appoint a worker representative, and implement the notice within the specified deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board authorization is required for an ISIC 7020 foreign market entry consultancy and regulatory licensing agency operating from an office environment. The sole governmental entities with jurisdiction are the New Zealand Companies Office (for registration) and the territorial authority (for commercial premises compliance). The company is not engaged in the manufacture, processing, or storage of goods subject to the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017 or the Trade in Endangered Species Act 1989.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the business does not require a New Zealand operational or manufacturing permit; the appropriate licences are the Certificate of Incorporation and the Building Warrant of Fitness for the registered office, plus the New Zealand Companies Register record. If the consultancy later undertakes regulated advisory activities such as immigration advice, financial advice, or legal services, separate licenses would be required under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007, the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, or the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 respectively.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, in coordination with the territorial authority and regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA); note that the RMA is being replaced by the Natural and Built Environment Act 2023, but the EIA screening process remains administratively active
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Full EIA Report not required. An office-based business consultancy under ISIC 7020 does not constitute a 'prohibited activity', 'discretionary activity', or 'controlled activity' for which an application for resource consent or an assessment of environmental effects (AEE) would be mandatory. No activity listed in the Fourth Schedule of the Resource Management Act 1991 (large-scale industrial developments) is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A — zero discharge and zero emissions business activity. The registered office produces no wastewater beyond domestic sewage, no volatile organic compounds (VOCs) beyond trace office cleaning solvents, and no hazardous waste. Compliance thresholds under the RMA and regional plans: the office must connect to the public wastewater system only, municipal solid waste disposal must be contracted to a licensed waste collector in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, and the use of cleaning solvents must comply with the approved New Zealand Product Safety Standards (if any).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, including a compliant fire evacuation scheme where the office occupies a high-occupancy building and annual fire safety inspection certification; structural load inspections and a current Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004 issued by the territorial authority; workplace clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 including the WorkSafe general duty of care, registration of the principal place of business with WorkSafe where applicable, completion of an asbestos or hazardous building material assessment for pre-1980 premises, and maintenance of an electrical safety certificate (Regulation 16 of the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010) for permanent electrical installations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Tāke); online portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity with no New Zealand tax nexus has no compulsory IRD number obligation. If the International Company carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, exceeds the GST registration threshold, or voluntarily registers for GST, the non-resident company must first obtain an IRD number. Application is made via myIR or by filing form IR742 (IRD number application for a non-resident company), attaching the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director details, and certified proof of identity. Once the IRD number is issued, GST registration is completed through the myIR 'GST registration' service, selecting a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing cycle. Non-resident suppliers of cross-border remote services may use the simplified offshore GST registration portal. The IRD number serves as the single statutory TIN and GST/VAT identification number; New Zealand does not issue a separate VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no check-the-box entity classification election and no general elective pass-through regime. Available statutory elections relevant to this structure include GST grouping under sections 55 to 55C of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, GST branch registration under section 58A, provisional tax payment options, and certain withholding tax and portfolio investment allocation rules. Hybrid mismatch and branch mismatch rules under sections FH 1 to FH 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007 apply automatically and are not elective; taxpayers may however arrange inter-company payments and transfer pricing positions to ensure the rules do not neutralise deductible outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a broad-based value-added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 gross turnover in a 12-month period; non-resident suppliers of cross-border remote services to New Zealand consumers are subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold and may use simplified registration for offshore suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or mandatory digital stamping system. Electronic invoicing is legally valid and accepted by IRD on a records-retention basis. The government promotes Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 through a voluntary national e-invoicing framework, and central government agencies are required to receive e-invoices via Peppol; however, no general mandate applies to private-sector suppliers. There is no API-based pre-clearance requirement for ordinary GST invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rating under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 applies where goods are physically exported by the supplier from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply and the supplier holds the prescribed export documentation. For services, zero-rating under section 11A applies where the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, the services are not directly in connection with land or movable property located in New Zealand, and the supply is not a supply to a New Zealand consumer. For overseas market-entry consultancy supplied by the International Company to non-resident commercial clients, zero-rating is available when the recipient is contractually a non-resident company, the consultancy is performed and delivered offshore or via electronic communications to a recipient located outside New Zealand, the advice is consumed wholly outside New Zealand, and the supplier retains sufficient evidence of non-resident status and offshore usage. Services physically supplied to a person present in New Zealand, or digital services supplied to private consumers in New Zealand, remain subject to 15% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing foreign currency repatriation
Signed service contract identifying the non-resident recipient
Non-resident status evidence (overseas tax registration, incorporation certificate, or equivalent)
Deliverable and performance records demonstrating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD may deny zero-rating and claw back output GST, input credits, and refunds if export documentation is incomplete, the non-resident status of the recipient is not substantiated, or the services are found to be consumed in New Zealand. Shortfall penalties apply at 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion, together with use-of-money interest running from the original GST due date. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims may also subject directors and officers to criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994, including significant fines and imprisonment, with retrospective recovery unlimited by the normal four-year adjustment period in cases of evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as the central monetary and prudential authority, with the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) within Land Information New Zealand administering capital-account foreign investment screening; there is no separate foreign-exchange control administration and the Reserve Bank does not require exchange-control permits for current or capital account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full Article VIII currency convertibility. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely floating and fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. There is no exchange-control regime restricting inbound equity, inbound loans, dividend repatriation, royalty remittance, or settlement of service fees. Practical hurdles are non-exchange based: (i) non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) of 15% on dividends and royalties, reduced by applicable double-tax treaties and subject to New Zealand imputation credit rules for dividends; (ii) OIO consent requirements for transactions that involve 'sensitive land' or 'significant business assets' (acquisition of 25% or more ownership / control of an entity with assets over NZD 100 million or turnover over NZD 200 million, or in specified sensitive sectors); and (iii) AML/CFT verification requirements under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. A low-risk consultancies business model involving overseas market-entry advisory fees is treated as ordinary current-account trade in services and faces no convertibility or remittance restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no statutory conversion timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts and foreign-currency earnings may be retained indefinitely in NZD or foreign-currency bank accounts without restriction. The only obligations are statistical and regulatory in nature: banks submit aggregated balance-of-payments reporting on flows exceeding NZD 50,000, and prescribed transaction reporting under the AML/CFT Act applies to wire transfers at or above NZD 10,000.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with trade finance lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as a secondary settlement rail for low-risk consultancy disbursements, subject to licensing constraints. Wise (formerly TransferWise) is registered on New Zealand's Financial Service Providers Register (FSP) and operates through partner banks; Airwallex is likewise FSP-registered in New Zealand. These digital/EMI platforms are reliable for sub-NZD 250,000 cross-border B2B payments and provide competitive FX pricing. They are not licensed New Zealand banks and therefore cannot hold capital escrow balances, issue commercial letters of credit, or provide borrowings-based treasury facilities. Legal constraint: accepting funds or conducting money remittance in New Zealand requires compliance with the AML/CFT Act as a 'financial institution', and taking deposits other than through a licensed bank is prohibited under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. For capital escrow and major trade settlements, tier-1 licensed bank rails remain mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring physical director attendance for account opening, but most tier-1 banks require in practice at least one natural-person director who is a New Zealand tax resident or an NZ-registered office presentation, or a physical interview at the bank's corporate banking centre (typically Auckland or Christchurch) for wholly offshore boards. Remote and hybrid onboarding is permitted under the RBNZ-supervised AML/CFT framework: the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Identity Verification) Regulations 2011 allow non-face-to-face verification through dual-source electronic checks (e.g., passport combined with a bank statement or utility bill, certified by a notary public or a registered bank officer). Practical hybrid structure: offshore directors complete certified document lodgement and video identity attestation, while the New Zealand registered agent physically presents the certificate of incorporation, register of directors, and company seal/statutory declarations at the bank branch. The absence of a physical interview mandate is thus conditional on the completeness of the certified corporate KYC pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly offshore board of directors with no New Zealand revenue footprint, operating as an International Company under a tax-exempt zone classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of certificate of incorporation and memorandum/articles of association; certified register of directors and shareholders; proof of New Zealand registered office from a licensed registered office provider; signed statutory declaration of source of funds; audited or management financial statements of the ultimate parent group; a current corporate intelligence report (e.g., Dun & Bradstreet) demonstrating no adverse history; board resolution authorising the account opening; and a structured explanation of the tax-exempt zone status with supporting legal opinion from New Zealand counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Prescribed transaction (wire transfer at or above NZD 10,000) or an unexpected large third-party inbound payment that does not match the declared business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retain the signed engagement contract for overseas market-entry consultancy; itemised invoice referencing ISIC 7020/NAICS 541611 services; the underlying feasibility-study deliverable or progress report; KYC file for the remitting client; balance-of-payments purpose code specifying 'management and consulting services'; and contemporaneous correspondence with the remitting bank evidencing the commercial rationale and absence of layering or structured payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction routing involving restricted or regulated industries, including clients with foreign-regulatory-licensing or government-procurement exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written legal opinion confirming that overseas market-entry consulting and regulatory licensing agency services are not licensable financial services in New Zealand; ISIC v4 (7020) and NAICS 2022 (541611) classification certificates; a business scope descriptor approved by the NZ Companies Office; a compliance and ethical-risk policy manual; and a sanctions/PEPS screening report on the underlying client showing no matches with OFAC/EU/UN lists and no politically exposed persons without senior-management approval.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound equity capital is via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas parent or shareholder to the New Zealand entity's tier-1 bank account. The remittance must be classified for balance-of-payments purposes as 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (BOP component 5200 series), not as a loan, when funding subscription of shares; a capital-escrow contribution should be referenced with the purpose code 'Corporate Treasury – Capital Contribution'. Supporting documents required by the receiving bank: board resolution approving the capital injection; shareholder subscription letter or share allotment certificate; a certificate of incumbency from the jurisdiction of origin; and beneficial-ownership declarations for any natural person holding 25% or more of the entity. Inbound amounts above NZD 50,000 trigger the receiving bank's prescribed transaction verification and potential enhanced due diligence, but require no exchange-control approval from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand unless an OIO consent threshold is met (not applicable to a consultancy with no sensitive land and asset values below OIO thresholds).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade disbursements is SWIFT MT103 for direct cash payments to overseas consultants, vendors, and licensing agents, using standard SWIFT/BIC and IBAN-equivalent beneficiary identifiers and an appropriate purpose code (e.g., 'Business services fees'). For higher-value trade-related settlements with documentary evidence, a commercial letter of credit issued under UCP600 via MT700 is permissible; given the consultancy's services-natured business, a standby letter of credit (MT760) or bank guarantee is more practical to secure performance obligations. Domestic NZD legs within New Zealand clear through the local high-value clearing system (ISO 20022-compliant payments infrastructure), while cross-border FX conversion is executed by the bank on its dealing desk at wholesale rates, with optional same-day or value-tomorrow settlement. All outbound wires above NZD 10,000 are subject to AML/CFT prescribed-transaction reporting and, where destined to high-risk jurisdictions, enhanced screening against sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (up to 24-month tenors) for NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, and NZD/EUR exposures incurred on overseas consultancy fees and parent funding flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies where the consultancy invoices clients in currencies such as CNY, KRW, or INR, and where no deliverable funding exists in those currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to align NZD-denominated capital or intercompany funding with USD or AUD advisory contract proceeds, managing term and floating-rate basis risk

FX options (plain vanilla calls/puts, zero-cost collars, and knock-in structures) transacted under wholesale investor exemptions, requiring the counterparty to be a licensed New Zealand bank or an FMA-qualified derivatives issuer under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return pursuant to section 208, Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies; Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the anniversary date of incorporation (the annual return date); electronic filing may be submitted up to 3 months before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 200 (approximately USD 120); if no annual return is filed for 6 months or more, the Registrar may issue a removal notice and strike the company off the New Zealand register; reinstatement requires a court or Registrar order with additional costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and tax-exempt status confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date, the return is due by 7 July and terminal tax is due by 7 February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (initial NZD 250 with escalating daily and monthly penalties, plus use-of-money interest); continued default may trigger IRD enforcement actions, asset restriction notices, and compromise of the tax-exempt certificate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and independent audit report (if the company exceeds the 'large' threshold or a 5% shareholder requests an audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (filed with or adjacent to the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the annual return date if mandatory filing applies; otherwise, financial statements must be prepared within 5 months of the balance date and retained for 7 years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NZD 200 late filing penalty per return, plus daily director penalties and offence liability under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; persistent non-filing can be a ground for deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT annual beneficial ownership verification and registered agent compliance certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Supervised registered business group under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (internal agent record, not filed with the Companies Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, reconciled within 20 working days after the annual return date or upon any change in ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisory interventions including formal warnings, remediation directions, and civil penalty orders up to NZD 2 million; failure to maintain current UBO data invalidates the agent's certification and may compromise the tax-exempt status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, i.e., it fails any one of the following three exemption tests at balance date: total assets of NZD 60 million or less, total revenue of NZD 30 million or less, and fewer than 50 full-time-equivalent employees. An audit is also triggered by a valid request from shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting rights.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1, full IFRS); NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2, RDR); Tier 3/4 simplified NZ GAAP for very small entities; tax-exempt international company status does not displace the applicable financial reporting standard.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return to the Companies Office requires certification that the register of members and the register of directors are accurate as at the annual return date. The registered agent must verify and record ultimate beneficial ownership for each shareholder holding 5% or more of issued capital, applying customer due diligence standards under the AML/CFT Act 2009. Any share transfer must be entered in the register within 10 working days; an annual confirmation of unchanged UBO is executed by the agent and retained in the company's on-site records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registered Office register and address-for-service record
Certified Minute Book (board and shareholder resolutions)
Register of Charges (if any encumbrances exist)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 - 1,800 per annum (registered office, corporate secretarial/agent services, and annual return filing)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 9,000 for a full NZ IFRS audit; USD 2,000 - 4,000 for a review engagement where the company qualifies for streamlined assurance

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for standard consultancy income. The only material preferential concession is the refundable R&D tax credit of 15% on eligible research and development expenditure, which is structural and does not constitute a reduced headline rate. The entity's internal 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' classification is not an Inland Revenue designation; if the entity is a New Zealand resident company, the 28% corporate rate applies to worldwide income unless a specific exemption in the Income Tax Act 2007 is engaged.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to shareholder continuity and same-business continuity tests under ss IA 4–IA 6 of the Income Tax Act 2007)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 – Annual Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically via IRD's myIR portal or through a commercial e-filing tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the return must be filed by 7 July of the same calendar year. For non-standard balance dates, the statutory deadline is the 7th day of the second month after the balance date. A tax agent may obtain an extension to a later date under the IRD's extension regime if the taxpayer is not in arrears.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income from business activities, including consultancy fees, feasibility study income, and licensing agency revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company carrying on business in New Zealand must report only New Zealand-sourced income. Income from overseas market entry consulting is sourced to the market where services are performed and where the client benefits; DTA tie-breaker rules may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses and deductions attributed to earning the assessable income, including salaries, contractor fees, travel, research, and regulatory licensing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses are deductible to the extent they are incurred in deriving New Zealand assessable income. For a non-resident company, foreign-sourced overheads must be apportioned under s DA 2 and IRD's apportionment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (assessable income minus deductions) before adjustments, excluding imputation credits and depreciation claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use New Zealand accounting concepts, adjusted for tax purposes. Foreign exchange gains from Wise B2B or bank wire settlements must be recognised if of a revenue nature.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends received from New Zealand resident companies and any withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may be entitled to claim a credit for New Zealand resident withholding tax and NRWT deducted at source; a tax treaty may reduce the credit available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid during the income year under the three-instalment protocol.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with New Zealand PE income are required to pay provisional tax in the same instalment cycle. Relief may be available under DTA provisions for payroll taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable or refund due (28% of Box 3 less credits from Box 4 and Box 5, adjusted for any R&D tax credit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax payable is calculated on the New Zealand taxable income only. Refunds are paid to the non-resident company's New Zealand bank account or directed via bank wire after IRD validation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for the first month the IR4 is overdue, plus NZ$50 for each subsequent month it remains overdue, capped at NZ$500. For large taxpayers, the monthly penalties are increased to NZ$500. In addition, late payment penalties of 1% per month on unpaid tax and use-of-money interest under s 139A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 accrue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional tax instalment payments – no separate return form; payments are recorded through myIR using the 'standard uplift' method or the 'estimation' method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date, the provisional tax instalments are due on 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May of the following income year. Non-standard balance dates use the 5th day of the month following the corresponding standard instalment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First provisional tax payment, typically 1/3 of the residual income tax liability from the prior year uplifted by 105%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must use the uplift method based on the New Zealand residual income tax; an estimated method is permitted with proper justification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Second provisional tax payment, bringing the cumulative paid amount to 2/3 of the annual estimate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any large New Zealand PE can adjust the estimate; underpayment triggers use-of-money interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final provisional tax instalment, equalising the total provisional tax paid with the annual residual income tax, plus any additional top-up.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final top-up is payable on the IR4 due date. Non-resident companies must ensure the tax is paid before departure of the responsible director to avoid collection difficulties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment penalty of 1% per month on the unpaid amount for each month overdue, capped at 25% of the tax payable, plus use-of-money interest under s 139A. If provisional tax is underpaid by more than the accepted tolerance, an additional penalty of 5% may apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (standard non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder). A reduced rate of 5% may apply to fully imputed dividends if the company has notified a 5% dividend withholding rate; a 0% DWR is possible for fully imputed dividends paid to a resident of a DTA partner where the shareholding threshold is met. The statutory default rate remains 30% for non-notifying companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) the beneficial owner must obtain a certificate of residence from its home tax authority (e.g., US Form 6166, Australian TRC, UK tax residence certificate); (2) submit the certificate to the New Zealand payer before the payment date together with a completed IRD Form IR441 'Notice of Variation of NRWT' or the payer's own variation system; (3) the payer must be satisfied that the beneficial owner is resident and meets any limitation-of-benefits clause; (4) if the full 30% rate was withheld, the non-resident recipient must file an IR3NR return and attach the certificate of residence to claim a refund of the excess; (5) IRD may request additional evidence of economic substance for low-tax-residence jurisdictions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties is 15%; DTA treaties commonly reduce this to 10% for patents, know-how trademarks, and copyright. Statutory NRWT on interest is 15%; a 10% rate applies for certain portfolio interest under approved issuer levy (AIL) alternative of 2% if the payer elects AIL. DTA reductions can lower interest NRWT to 10% or 0% for non-associated borrowers depending on the treaty partner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File equivalent) is mandated by section GC 12 of the Income Tax Act 2007 when: (a) the taxpayer is a 'large taxpayer' (annual gross income of the taxpayer or its group exceeding NZ$30,000,000), and (b) the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZ$1,000,000 in the income year. A Master File may be requested for multinational groups with consolidated revenue over NZ$100,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) framework akin to the BVI or Cayman regimes. However, the Commissioner of Inland Revenue applies a substance-over-form doctrine through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007; (ii) the extended definition of 'tax residence' in section YD 4, which looks to incorporation, head office, and centre of management; (iii) permanent establishment and branch profit attribution rules for non-residents; and (iv) the 'artificial arrangement' rule in section GB 1. A shell company lacking real presence and staff in New Zealand is exposed to full NZ residency, PE attribution, and GAAR recharacterisation. If the entity is an offshore International Company resident in the Cook Islands, the Cook Islands ESR 2019 requires economic substance for relevant activities, including consultancy and licensing operations, within that jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to declare New Zealand-sourced market entry consultancy fees, channelling payments through undisclosed Wise B2B business accounts or bank wires, or using bearer shares/nominee directors to conceal beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994: a fine of up to NZ$50,000 for an individual and NZ$100,000 for a body corporate, and imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years. In addition, a shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the resulting tax shortfall for evasion, plus use-of-money interest under section 139A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and shortfall penalties under section 149A TAA. Asset preservation orders and travel restrictions may be imposed against directors who attempt to leave New Zealand while tax is outstanding; custodial sentences apply for deliberate evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into a non-arm's-length cross-border arrangement with a related foreign entity for advisory or commission services, or paying excessive royalties/intercompany management fees from a New Zealand branch to a low-tax affiliate to reduce New Zealand taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may adjust the consideration to an arm's-length value under Subpart GC. Shortfall penalties under s 141A of the Tax Administration Act: 20% for failing to take reasonable care; 40% for an unacceptable tax position or abusive tax position; up to 100% for evasion. Use-of-money interest accrues on adjusted tax. The adjustment may be complemented by an equivalent compensating adjustment under the applicable DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved a transfer pricing policy lacking commercial substance can be assessed personally for penalties if they were knowingly involved in the tax shortfall. In egregious cases, civil damages in a shareholder or tax authority winding-up action, director disqualification, and an interdiction order preventing removal of funds from New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox or conduit entity in New Zealand with no full-time staff, physical premises, or demonstrable commercial activity while claiming the benefits of the NZ residence status and the DTA network, or utilising a Cook Islands International Company without substance in its claimed tax-exempt jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deemed tax residency under s YD 4 bringing worldwide income into the NZ tax net; application of s BG 1 GAAR to recharacterise the entire arrangement; penalties for failure to file resident returns; and possible deregistration for non-trading under the Companies Act 1993. If the entity is an offshore exempt entity, the Cook Islands Economic Substance Regulations may impose a financial penalty of USD 10,000–100,000 and imprisonment for directors for false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for company taxes where they knowingly cause the company to use shell status to defeat tax. Civil liability for unpaid taxes, travel bans, and disqualification as a director for up to 5 years under the Companies Act; in serious cases, imprisonment for obtaining tax advantages by fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting client funds through Wise B2B or bank wire without implementing a risk-based customer due diligence programme, failing to verify ultimate beneficial owners, or failing to report suspicious transactions when providing market entry consultancy that overlaps with financial advisory or money transmission activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 of up to NZ$2,000,000 for a serious breach by a reporting entity and NZ$500,000 for an individual; suspension or revocation of an MSB licence; criminal prosecution for money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961, punishable by imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers who knowingly engage in money laundering or tolerate deferred-dawn reporting obligations face personal criminal liability and imprisonment. They may also be ordered to pay reparations to victims and be subject to asset freezes and international travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Restructuring repatriation of profits to a foreign parent as interest, management fees, or a loan repayment rather than as a dividend in order to avoid the 30% NRWT on dividends, and without substantive debt or services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under s GB 1/GA 1 with full NRWT imposed at 30%; shortfall penalty of 20% for not taking reasonable care, 40% for an unacceptable tax position, or up to 100% if evasion is established; use-of-money interest and late payment penalties apply from the original distribution date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid NRWT under s 167 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 if the company fails to deduct or pay withholding tax, and they can be prosecuted for a knowing failure to pay tax deductions. Civil restitution to the Tax Commissioner and prohibition from leaving the jurisdiction are available remedies.
